chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not hire a Zoroastrian woman for breastfeeding your child, but hire for him a Jewish or Christian woman, and they must not drink wine and you must prevent them from doing so.

key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيَّةَ: The Zoroastrian woman (female follower of Magism)

ai.seo_question: Which religious groups are permitted or prohibited as wet nurses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes a hierarchy of religious affinity in wet-nursing, prioritizing People of the Book over Zoroastrians, reflecting the Shia juristic view that their monotheism offers greater spiritual safety for the child. The specific condition of abstaining from wine highlights the practical concern of preserving the child's religious upbringing and purity from major impurities associated with their practices.
